chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A child is not born to us except that we name him Muhammad. So when seven days have passed for us, if we wish, we change [the name], and if we wish, we leave it [as is].

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (a title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Seven days (a period often associated with naming ceremonies in Islamic tradition)

ai.seo_question: What is the practice of the Imams regarding naming their children initially and after seven days?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam's preference for the name Muhammad, reflecting the high status of the Prophet in Shia tradition, while demonstrating the flexibility in naming conventions during the initial week. The seven-day period aligns with the timing of the 'Aqiqah sacrifice, indicating that the final name selection is often coupled with this ritual act. This practice underscores the balance between adhering to prophetic traditions and exercising personal discretion in familial matters.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There does not get born a child for us<sup>asws</sup> except that we<sup>asws</sup> name it as Muhammad. So when seven days pass for us<sup>asws</sup>, so if we<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, we<sup>asws</sup> changed it, and if we<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, we<sup>asws</sup> leave it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of our people from those whom he has mentioned who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
We name every child born to us Muhammad and after seven days if we like we change or keep the same name.’”
